Fact.Name: Income source options
Fact.Description: Options describing the source of a member's income.

Fact.Name: Household members
Fact.Description: List of household members

Fact.Name: Incomes
Fact.Description: List of incomes received by household members

Fact.Name: Member
Fact.Description: The household member to whom this income belongs

Fact.Name: Income type
Fact.Description: The source/type of this income.

Fact.Name: Monthly amount
Fact.Description: The monthly amount of this income.

Fact.Name: Parent-child relationships
Fact.Description: List of parent-or-caregiver relationships between household members. Each entry links one adult to one child and covers either (a) a natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship or (b) a non-parent household member who exercises parental control over the child. A single child may appear in multiple entries (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Parent / caregiver
Fact.Description: The household member who is either a natural, adoptive, or stepparent in this relationship, or a non-parent household member exercising parental control over the child. When the relationship is a natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship to a child aged twenty-one (21) years or younger living in the same home, this member must be included in the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Child
Fact.Description: The household member who is the child in this relationship — either the natural, adoptive, or stepchild of the parent, or a child under the parental control of a non-parent household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is non-parent parental-control relationship
Fact.Description: Whether this relationship is the non-parent caregiver kind (the child is under the parental control of an adult who is not their natural, adoptive, or stepparent), rather than a natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship. A child under eighteen (18) is considered to be under parental control of a household member when financially or otherwise dependent on that member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Parent provides more than half of physical care
Fact.Description: Whether the parent-side member in this relationship is responsible for more than half of the physical care of the child. Used by the SNAP student-eligibility exemption for a student responsible for the physical care of a dependent household member aged six (6) to under twelve (12) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Adequate childcare is unavailable
Fact.Description: Whether the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available for the child-side member in this relationship to enable the parent-side member to attend class and satisfy the requirement of item B or item C of 4.306.1 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Age
Fact.Description: Age of this member in years

Fact.Name: Has physical disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a physical disability

Fact.Name: Has mental disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a mental disability

Fact.Name: Receives SSI or disability/blindness payments
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits under Title XVI of the Social Security Act, or the Colorado Supplement, or Aid to the Needy and Disabled-Supplemental Security Income-Colorado Supplement (AND-SSI-CS), or Aid to the Blind-Supplemental Security Income-Colorado Supplement (AB-SSI-CS); or Disability or Blindness Payments under Title I, II, X, or IXV of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran with service-connected or non-service-connected disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a veteran with a service-connected disability rated or paid as a total disability under Title 38 of the United States Code, or is a veteran receiving a pension for a non-service-connected disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently housebound
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a veteran considered by the Veterans Affairs (VA) to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound under Title 38 of the United States Code (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran's surviving spouse or child needing aid and attendance
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a surviving spouse of a veteran and considered in need of aid and attendance or permanently housebound, or a surviving child of a veteran and considered by the VA to be permanently incapable of self-support under Title 38 of the United States Code (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran's surviving spouse or child with permanent disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a surviving spouse or child of a veteran considered by the VA to be entitled to compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a non-service-connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code, and has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act. "Entitled" refers to those veterans' surviving spouses and children who are receiving the compensation or benefits or have been approved for such benefits but are not yet receiving them (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives public disability retirement pension
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act and receives a federal, state, or local public disability retirement pension (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives railroad retirement disability annuity
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives an annuity for disability from the railroad retirement board and is considered as a person with disabilities by the SSA, or qualifies for Medicare as determined by the railroad retirement board (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives interim assistance pending SSI/disability benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a recipient of interim assistance benefits pending the receipt of Supplemental Security Income (SSI), disability-related medical assistance under Title XIX of the Social Security Act, or disability-based state assistance benefits, provided that eligibility for those benefits is based on disability or blindness criteria at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets any of the criteria defining a "person with disabilities" under SNAP: receipt of SSI or other disability/blindness payments; veteran status with a service-connected or non-service-connected disability; veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently housebound; surviving spouse or child of a veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently incapable of self-support; surviving spouse or child of a veteran with a permanent disability; permanent disability with a public disability retirement pension; railroad retirement disability annuity; or interim assistance pending SSI or disability-based benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is boarder
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with others and pays reasonable compensation to others for lodging and meals (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is roomer
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an individual to whom a household furnishes lodging, but not meals, for compensation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in boarding house
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in an establishment that is licensed as a commercial enterprise and which offers meals and lodging for compensation, as described in 7 C.F.R 273.1(b)(3)(i) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in an institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in a place which has not been authorized by FNS to accept SNAP benefits, but which provides its residents with more than fifty percent (50%) of their daily meals as part of its normal services. Residents of a halfway house for persons with a disability are residents of an institution if they are provided meals as part of their regular service. Students who purchase meal plans through an institution of higher education are residents of an institution if the meal plan provides them more than fifty percent (50%) of their meals (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: Lives in federally subsidized housing for persons aged 60 and older
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of federally subsidized housing for persons aged sixty (60) and older under 12 U.S.C. 1701Q or 12 U.S.C. 1715Z-1 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Resides at a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation facility
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a narcotic addict or alcoholic, or the child of one, who resides at a facility or treatment center for purposes of regular participation in a drug or alcoholic treatment and rehabilitation program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Resident of a homeless shelter
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of a public or private nonprofit shelter for the homeless (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Exempt from boarding house or institution disqualification
Fact.Description: Whether this member, although a resident of a boarding house or institution, qualifies for an exemption under Section 4.304.41 that allows them to participate in SNAP. The exemptions are: (A) resident of federally subsidized housing for persons aged 60 and older under 12 U.S.C. 1701Q or 1715Z-1; (B) narcotic addicts or alcoholics and their children residing at a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation facility; (C) blind or disabled residents of a public or private nonprofit group living arrangement facility; (D) women, or women and their children, temporarily residing in a public or private nonprofit shelter for battered women and children; (E) residents of public or private nonprofit shelters for the homeless (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Prepares food with household
Fact.Description: Whether this member customarily purchases and prepares food together with the rest of the household for home consumption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in group living arrangement
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in a public or private non-profit facility certified under Section 1616(e) of the Social Security Act which serves no more than sixteen (16) people (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is live-in attendant
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with the household to provide child-care or other personal services (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is separate and apart
Fact.Description: Whether this member, who would otherwise be a mandatory household member, has established a residence separate and apart from the other mandatory household members. A residence is only considered established as separate and apart when the individual pays shelter expenses, supports the maintenance of the other residence (e.g., paying rent/mortgage, utilities, insurance, or other charges necessary to maintain the residence), or has provided that separate address to other governmental organizations or an employer as their primary residence. When true, the member is not required to be considered part of the SNAP household, and any monies that person provides to the SNAP household should be considered unearned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member who must be considered in the same household as the other mandatory individuals they live with, even if they declare they do not customarily purchase and prepare their food together for home consumption. Mandatory members include the designated head of household, anyone in a spouse relationship with another household member, any mandatory child, any parent of a mandatory child living in the same home, and any person aged sixty (60) or older with a disability who is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals and lives with others whose income exceeds 165% of the federal poverty line (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.203, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is optional household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an optional household member who resides with the household but shall not be considered a household member in determining the household's eligibility or allotment, unless otherwise stated. True when this member is eligible to be in a separate household as a person aged sixty (60) or older with a disability whose food-preparation-group co-residents' combined income does not exceed 165% of the federal poverty line, when this member is a foster child whom the foster parent may choose to include in or exclude from the SNAP household, or when this member is a boarder whom the household may choose to include as a household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1, 4.304.3).

Fact.Name: Is boarder
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a boarder of the client's household. Boarders are only considered members of a client's SNAP household if the household requests that they be considered household members (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is non-household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with the household but shall not be considered a household member in determining the household's eligibility or allotment, unless otherwise stated in 4.304.3. True when this member is a roomer or a live-in attendant. Boarders are excluded here because they are essentially optional household members — see /members/*/isOptionalHouseholdMember (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.31).

Fact.Name: Is part of household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is part of the SNAP household — a group of individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare food together for home consumption. Mandatory household members are always considered part of the household regardless of food preparation. A member who would otherwise be part of the household but has established a residence separate and apart (/members/*/isSeparateAndApart) is excluded (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is head of household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is the head of the SNAP household — the person to whom the local office addresses correspondence and notices about the household's case, generally the individual who completes the application process and is responsible for obtaining and using the household's EBT card (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304).

Fact.Name: Spouse
Fact.Description: The household member who is this member's spouse — either a person married to this member under state law, or a person living together with this member who is free to marry and is representing themselves as a spouse to relatives, friends, neighbors, or the larger community (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory spouse
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a spouse relationship with another member of the household who is themselves part of the SNAP household. True when this member's spouseId references a household member who is part of the household, or when another member who is part of the household identifies this member as their spouse. Spouses must always be considered part of the same SNAP household regardless of whether they purchase and prepare food together (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is emancipated minor
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a minor who has been emancipated as defined by state law. An emancipated minor is not considered to be under another household member's parental control for purposes of the mandatory-child SNAP household rule (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is foster child
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a foster child. Foster children are explicitly excluded from the rule requiring a child under eighteen (18) who lives under the parental control of a non-parent household member to be a mandatory household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Mandatory child age limit (parent case)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) on a child's age for the first mandatory-child SNAP household case: a person aged twenty-one (21) years or younger living with their natural, adoptive, or stepparent (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Mandatory child age limit (parental control case)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on a child's age for the second mandatory-child SNAP household case: a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age living with and under the parental control of a non-parent household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child via parent in household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the first mandatory-child case: a person aged twenty-one (21) years or younger who has at least one /parentChildRelationships entry whose parent-side member is part of the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child via non-parent parental control
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the second mandatory-child case: a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age who has at least one /parentChildRelationships entry of the non-parent caregiver kind (isNonparentParentalControl is true) whose parent-side member is part of the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household as the child of, or a child under the parental control of, another household member. True when either /members/*/isMandatoryChildViaParent or /members/*/isMandatoryChildViaParentalControl is true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent via child in household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the parent-side mirror of the first mandatory-child case: a natural, adoptive, or stepparent (i.e., the linked /parentChildRelationships entry has isNonparentParentalControl false) of a household member aged twenty-one (21) years or younger who is themselves part of the SNAP household. Uses childId/isPartOfHousehold on the child side so the existence-in-household check matches the policy phrasing "living with their natural or adoptive parent(s) or stepparent(s)" (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent via non-parent parental control
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the parent-side mirror of the second mandatory-child case: a non-parent caregiver (the linked /parentChildRelationships entry has isNonparentParentalControl true) over a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age who is themselves part of the SNAP household. Uses childId/isPartOfHousehold on the child side so the existence-in-household check matches the policy phrasing "living with…a household member" (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household as the parent of, or non-parent caregiver exercising parental control over, a child who is themselves part of the SNAP household. True when either /members/*/isMandatoryParentViaChild or /members/*/isMandatoryParentViaParentalControl is true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is unable to purchase and prepare own meals due to a disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is experiencing a disability and, as a result of that disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals. Used together with age sixty (60) or older to determine when the member must be considered part of the same SNAP household as the others they live with (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Others in food-prep group have income exceeding 165% FPL
Fact.Description: Whether the combined income of every other member of this member's food-preparation group exceeds 165% of the federal poverty level for a household size equal to the food-preparation group's size minus this member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1). Placeholder pending the income calculation work.

Fact.Name: Is mandatory elderly member with disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household under the rule that a person aged sixty (60) or older who is also experiencing a disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals, prepares food with the rest of the household, and is residing with other individuals whose combined income exceeds 165% of the federal poverty line (for the food-preparation group's size excluding this member) must be in the same household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Can be separate elderly-with-disability household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is eligible to be considered a separate SNAP household under the rule that a person aged sixty (60) or older who is also experiencing a disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals, and is residing with other individuals whose combined income does not exceed 165% of the federal poverty line (for the food-preparation group's size excluding this member) can be in a separate household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Has ABAWD disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a physical or mental disability that disqualifies them from ABAWD status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD minimum age
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the ABAWD age range (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD maximum age
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) of the ABAWD age range (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: A household member younger than this age disqualifies others from ABAWD status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Under ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is younger than the ABAWD dependent age limit

Fact.Name: Has member under ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: Whether the household contains anyone younger than the ABAWD dependent age limit

Fact.Name: Is ABAWD
Fact.Description: Able-Bodied Adult Without Dependents: aged 18 through 54, without a physical or mental disability, in a household with no one under 18 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Application filing date
Fact.Description: The date an application for public assistance is received by the county office (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Application for recertification
Fact.Description: Whether this application was submitted prior to the last month of the certification period to determine the household's continued eligibility for the next certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Allotment
Fact.Description: The total amount of SNAP benefits the household is authorized to receive in a particular month, computed by rounding the unfloored allotment down to the nearest dollar, then raising it up to the federal minimum allotment for one- and two-person households (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Unfloored allotment
Fact.Description: The household's SNAP benefit allotment before rounding down to the nearest dollar or applying the minimum-benefit rule, computed as the maximum allotment for the household size minus thirty percent (30%) of net monthly income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Expected contribution rate
Fact.Description: The share of net monthly income the household is expected to contribute toward its food costs, used to compute the SNAP benefit allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Expected contribution
Fact.Description: The portion of the household's net monthly income that the household is expected to contribute toward its food costs, which is subtracted from the maximum allotment to determine the SNAP benefit (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Household size
Fact.Description: The number of members in the household, used to look up the maximum monthly SNAP allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 1-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 1-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 2-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 2-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 3-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 3-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 4-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 4-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 5-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 5-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 6-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 6-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 7-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 7-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 8-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for an 8-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment per additional person
Fact.Description: The amount added to the 8-person maximum monthly SNAP allotment for each additional household member beyond eight, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment
Fact.Description: The maximum monthly SNAP allotment for the household, derived from the cost of the thrifty food plan as defined by the FNS. The cost of that diet is the basis for uniform allotments for all households regardless of their actual composition (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Looked up from the household-size schedule effective October 1, 2025, with /maxAllotmentPerAdditionalPerson added for each member beyond eight.

Fact.Name: Days in application month
Fact.Description: The exact number of days in the calendar month in which the household applied for benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Application day of month
Fact.Description: The day of the month on which the household submitted its application for benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Is migrant or seasonal farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a migrant or seasonal farm worker who is in the job stream and whose break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Has migrant or seasonal farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether the household contains any migrant or seasonal farm worker who is in the job stream (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Received SNAP in the last 30 days
Fact.Description: Whether the household received SNAP benefits within the thirty (30) days preceding the current application. Used to determine whether a migrant or seasonal farm worker household's break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days, which exempts the household from initial-month allotment proration (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Prorated allotment
Fact.Description: The household's SNAP benefit level for the initial month of application, rounded down to the nearest dollar. If the calculation of benefits for the initial month yields an allotment of less than the federal minimum allotment, no benefits are issued to the household for the initial month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3 B).

Fact.Name: Unfloored prorated allotment
Fact.Description: The household's initial-month allotment before rounding down to the nearest dollar or applying the minimum-benefit cutoff, computed using the exact number of days in the calendar month: ((days in month + 1) - date of application) * full month's unfloored allotment / days in the application month. Migrant or seasonal farm worker households in the job stream whose break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days are exempt from proration and receive the full month unfloored allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Minimum allotment
Fact.Description: The minimum amount of benefits issued to one- and two-person households that are eligible for assistance, but whose issuance calculates to less than the federally prescribed minimum allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Effective October 1, 2025, the minimum monthly allotment for 1-2 person households is $24.

Fact.Name: Basic Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: A fixed deduction applied to a household that does not pay for heating or cooling and incurs at least two non-heating or non-cooling utility costs, such as electricity, water, sewer, trash, cooking fuel, or telephone (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Heating/Cooling Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: A fixed deduction applied to any household that incurs a heating or cooling expense (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: One Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: A fixed deduction given to any household that is not eligible to receive the HCUA or BUA and incurs only one non-heating or non-cooling utility expense, such as electricity, water, sewer, trash, or cooking fuel. The OUA is not allowed if the household's only utility expense is a telephone (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Non-telephone utility allowance
Fact.Description: The fixed deduction amount applied to a household whose only utility expense is something other than the expense for a telephone (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Receives LEAP
Fact.Description: Whether the household receives benefits from the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LEAP), the Colorado program designed to help low-income clients pay a portion of their winter heating costs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives BCE-qualifying benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives, or is authorized to receive, SSI, Colorado Works (CW), Old Age Pension (OAP), Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), or Aid to the Blind (AB). OAP, AND, and AB are captured under the Adult Financial cash grant (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: All members receive BCE-qualifying benefits
Fact.Description: Whether every household member receives, or is authorized to receive, SSI, Colorado Works (CW), Old Age Pension (OAP), Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), Aid to the Blind (AB), or a combination of these benefits. The CW, SSI, OAP, and/or AB program(s) need only to authorize benefits for the household to be considered for BCE. Clients who are authorized to receive a benefit from one or more of these programs, but who are not paid such benefits because the grant is less than a minimum benefit or the benefits are suspended or are being recouped, are still considered eligible. Households entitled to Medicaid only are not considered SSI or Title IV-A participants (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Has member receiving Family Preservation services
Fact.Description: Whether at least one household member receives services from the Family Preservation Program. This determination must be documented in the case record (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Disqualified for Basic Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household is disqualified from being considered under Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE) because any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Has Basic Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies for Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE): either all members receive (or are authorized to receive) SSI, Colorado Works, Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled, or Aid to the Blind, or at least one member receives services from the Family Preservation Program. A household cannot be considered under BCE if any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; if the household received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during the month; or if the household previously lost eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and must be considered under Standard Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: ECE gross income rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the gross income threshold for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ECE gross income threshold
Fact.Description: Two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, below which a household's combined gross income must fall to qualify for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives non-cash TANF or MOE service
Fact.Description: Whether the household has been authorized to receive a non-cash Temporary Assistance to Needy Families/Maintenance of Effort (TANF/MOE) funded service designed to further TANF Purpose Four (4) by "encouraging the formation and maintenance of two-parent families." Authorization is granted to households with combined gross income below two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for Expanded Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household is disqualified from being considered under Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE) because, at the time of application, any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Has Expanded Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE): the household has been authorized to receive a non-cash TANF/MOE funded service designed to further TANF Purpose Four (encouraging the formation and maintenance of two-parent families), which is granted to households with combined gross income below two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level. A household cannot be considered under ECE if any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; if the household received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during the month; or if the household previously lost eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and must be considered under Standard Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Standard Eligibility applies
Fact.Description: Whether Standard Eligibility (SE) rules shall be applied to the household. SE rules apply to households that include a member serving a disqualification for an IPV or fraud conviction; households that include a member convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; households that previously lost SNAP eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and are reapplying after losing eligibility; or households that do not meet the criteria to be considered under BCE or ECE rules (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Elderly age minimum
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the age range for being considered "aged sixty (60) and older" under SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is elderly
Fact.Description: Whether this member is aged sixty (60) or older (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is elderly or person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether this member is aged sixty (60) or older, or is a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Has member elderly or person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether the household includes a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Gross income test rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the gross income threshold for Standard Eligibility households that do not include a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Gross income threshold
Fact.Description: One hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, at or below which the combined gross income of an SE household without a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability must fall (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Meets gross income test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's combined gross income is at or below one hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Non-liquid resources
Fact.Description: The sum of non-liquid resources across all household members (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resources
Fact.Description: The household's total countable resources, the sum of each member's total resources (liquid plus non-liquid) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resource limit
Fact.Description: The maximum allowable countable resources for a household reviewed under Standard Eligibility rules, prescribed in Section 4.408 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Meets resource test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's countable resources are below the limit prescribed in Section 4.408 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Meets financial criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the financial criteria for Standard Eligibility: net income (after all applicable deductions) at or below one hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level and resources below the Section 4.408 limit; households that do not include a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability must additionally have combined gross income at or below one hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Has Standard Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies under Standard Eligibility (SE): SE rules apply to the household, the household meets the SE financial criteria, and the household meets the nonfinancial eligibility criteria set out in Section 4.300. The household is also disqualified for the month if it received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during that month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Eligibility category options
Fact.Description: The categories under which a household may be determined eligible for SNAP: Basic Categorical Eligibility (Bce), Expanded Categorical Eligibility (Ece), or Standard Eligibility (Se); Ineligible indicates the household does not qualify under any category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Eligibility category
Fact.Description: The category of eligibility under which the household is determined eligible for SNAP: Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE), Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE), or Standard Eligibility (SE); Ineligible if the household does not qualify under any category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206)

Fact.Name: Extended certification period
Fact.Description: The twenty-four (24) month certification period assigned to households that contain only members aged sixty (60) and older and/or with a disability and have no earned income at the time of certification (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Standard certification period
Fact.Description: The six (6) month certification period assigned to households that are not assigned the twenty-four (24) month certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Certification period
Fact.Description: The length, in months, of the period of time for which a household has been certified to receive benefits. A twenty-four (24) month certification period is assigned to households that contain only members aged sixty (60) and older and/or with a disability and have no earned income at the time of certification; all other households are assigned a six (6) month certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Countable months
Fact.Description: The number of countable months accrued by this member within the past 36 months. A countable month is a month in which an ABAWD received a full SNAP allotment but did not meet work requirements or have an exemption from those requirements. ABAWDs who accrue three countable months within a 36-month period become disqualified from SNAP unless they meet an exemption or ABAWD work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: D-SNAP active
Fact.Description: Whether the Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (D-SNAP) is active for the affected county, following a Presidential disaster declaration for individual assistance and at the county's discretion in coordination with the state SNAP office and FNS (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Temporary emergency active
Fact.Description: Whether a temporary emergency is active — an emergency caused by any natural or human-caused disaster, other than a major disaster declared by the President of the United States under the Disaster Relief Act of 1974, which is determined by FNS to have disrupted commercial channels of food distribution (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for IPV/fraud
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation/fraud (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Convicted of drug-related felony involving SNAP
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs. Drug-related felony has the same meaning as in 7 C.F.R. 273.11(m) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Failed to provide or obtain SSN
Fact.Description: Whether this member has failed to provide or obtain a Social Security Number (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is ineligible non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible non-citizen. Citizens and non-citizen nationals are potentially eligible for SNAP; other non-citizens are ineligible unless they are a qualified non-citizen who is exempt from the additional-condition requirement, a qualified non-citizen who meets one of the additional conditions, or fall in one of the classes of non-qualified non-citizens eligible for participation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Student ineligibility minimum age
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the age range subject to the SNAP student-eligibility rule. Persons aged seventeen (17) or under are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 1).

Fact.Name: Student ineligibility maximum age
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) of the age range subject to the SNAP student-eligibility rule. Persons aged fifty (50) or over are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 2).

Fact.Name: Student exemption work hours per week
Fact.Description: Minimum (inclusive) average hours worked per week for the SNAP student-eligibility employment exemption: twenty (20) hours per week, paid (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B). TODO: the self-employed branch additionally requires earnings after allowable business expenses equal to at least the federal minimum wage multiplied by twenty (20) hours — not yet modeled.

Fact.Name: Student exemption dependent member age limit
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the age of a dependent household member whose care qualifies a full-time student for the SNAP student-eligibility exemption: a dependent household member under the age of six (6) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Student exemption dependent child age limit (single-parent provision)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the age of a dependent child whose care qualifies a full-time, single-parent student for the SNAP student-eligibility exemption: a dependent child under age twelve (12) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education
Fact.Description: Whether this member is enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education. Persons enrolled less than half time, persons enrolled full time in schools or training programs that are not institutions of higher education, persons attending high school, and persons participating in an on-the-job training program (training in an employment environment, excluding internships, field work, or practical experience associated with a course of higher education) are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 3-6). Enrollment status begins on the first day of the school term of the institution of higher education and continues through normal periods of class attendance, vacation, and recess unless the student graduates, is suspended or expelled, drops out, or does not intend to register for the next normal school term (excluding summer session); for eligibility purposes enrollment starts when the student starts classes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, C).

Fact.Name: Meets student eligibility exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets at least one of the eight student-eligibility exemption criteria at 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1: A physically or mentally unfit for employment; B employed for an average of twenty (20) hours per week and paid for such employment; C participating in a state or federally financed work-study program; D responsible for the care of a dependent household member under age six (6), or a full-time student who is a single parent with responsibility for the care of a dependent child under age twelve (12) (the single-parent provision); E responsible for more than half of the physical care of a dependent household member aged six (6) to under twelve (12) where the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available; F receiving a Title IV-A TANF cash grant; G assigned to or placed in an institution of higher education through a WIOA, Employment First, Trade Act, other state/local employment-and-training, or JOBS program; H participating in an on-the-job training program.

Fact.Name: Is participating in work-study
Fact.Description: Whether this member is participating in a work-study program for purposes of the SNAP student eligibility exemption. The work-study shall be approved for the school term and the student shall anticipate working during that time. The student qualifies for this exemption the month the school term in which the work-study will occur begins or the month work-study is approved, whichever is later. The exemption continues until the end of the school term or until it becomes known that the student has refused an assignment. The exemption shall not continue between terms when there is a break of one (1) full month or longer unless the student is participating in work-study during the break (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is assigned to higher education through an employment and training program
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student assigned to or placed in an institution of higher education through a program under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), Employment First (EF), a program under Section 236 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2296), another program for the purpose of employment and training operated by the state or local government (program shall have at least one (1) component equivalent to the SNAP EF Program), or as a result of participating in the JOBS program under Title IV of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, G).

Fact.Name: Is full-time student
Fact.Description: Whether this member's /members/*/studentEnrollmentStatus is FullTime (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Has care of a dependent household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member has at least one /parentChildRelationships entry whose child-side member is part of the SNAP household and is under the age of six (6). This captures responsibility for the care of a dependent household member under age six for the SNAP full-time-student exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is single parent of a dependent child
Fact.Description: Whether this member has at least one /parentChildRelationships entry to a household child under age twelve (12) for whom this member is the only parent of any kind (natural, adoptive, stepparent, or non-parent caregiver) in the same SNAP household. Captures the single-parent provision of the SNAP full-time-student exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is student responsible for a dependent child
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student who has responsibility for the care of a dependent household member under the age of six (6); or as a full-time student who is a single parent with responsibility for the care of a dependent child under age twelve (12). The full-time requirement only applies to the single-parent leg; the under-six leg applies to any student. The single-parent provision applies in those situations where only one parent of any kind (natural, adoptive, stepparent, or non-parent caregiver) — regardless of marital status — is in the same SNAP household as the child; this subsumes the policy's separate parental-control branch (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is student responsible for physical care of a dependent child without adequate childcare
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student who is responsible for more than half of the physical care of a dependent household member who has reached the age of six (6) but is under the age of twelve (12), where the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available to enable the individual to attend class and satisfy the requirement of item B or item C of 4.306.1. Derived from any /parentChildRelationships entry where this member is the parent, the child is part of the SNAP household and aged six (6) to under twelve (12), and both per-relationship flags parentProvidesMoreThanHalfOfPhysicalCare and adequateChildcareUnavailable are true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Is in K-12
Fact.Description: Whether this member is attending a K-12 school (kindergarten through twelfth grade). Persons attending high school are not considered under SNAP student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 5).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible student
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible student. A person aged eighteen (18) through forty-nine (49) and enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education is ineligible to participate in the SNAP unless they meet one of the exemption criteria outlined at 4.306.1. Persons attending K-12 and persons participating in an on-the-job training program are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 5-6).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for failure to cooperate with work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for failure to cooperate with work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Voluntarily quit or reduced work effort
Fact.Description: Whether this member has voluntarily quit a job or reduced their work effort to less than 30 hours a week. Whether the quit or reduction was with good cause is captured separately on /members/*/voluntaryQuitReason (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.308).

Fact.Name: Voluntary quit reason options
Fact.Description: Options enumerating the good cause reasons under which a member's voluntary quit of employment or reduction in work hours is not subject to sanction under SNAP. The list is not exhaustive (the local office may recognize other reasons) but captures the categories called out in policy: discrimination by an employer; work demands or conditions that render continued employment unreasonable; acceptance of new employment or at-least-half-time enrollment in a recognized school, training program, or institution of higher education that requires leaving employment; another household member accepting employment or at-least-half-time enrollment in another county or political sub-division that requires the household to move; resignations by persons under sixty (60) recognized by the employer as retirement; resignation from employment that does not meet the suitable-employment criteria of 4.310.7; circumstances beyond the individual's control where accepted full-time employment did not materialize or resulted in less than thirty (30) hours per week or weekly earnings below the federal minimum wage times thirty (30); leaving a job in connection with patterns of employment in which workers frequently move from one employer to another (such as migrant farm labor or construction work); illness of the head of household; illness of another household member requiring the head of household's presence; a household emergency; the unavailability of transportation; an employer demanding a reduction in the participant's work effort or salary through no fault of the employee; and lack of adequate child care for children who have reached age six (6) but are under age twelve (12) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Voluntary quit reason
Fact.Description: The reason for this member's voluntary quit of employment or reduction in work hours from the list enumerated in /voluntaryQuitReasonOptions. Selecting one of the 4.308.1 enumerated good cause reasons indicates good cause; selecting Other indicates a reason was given but it does not fall within an enumerated good cause category and — combined with /members/*/voluntarilyQuitOrReducedWorkEffort — drives the ineligible-voluntary-quit determination (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible due to voluntary quit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is ineligible for SNAP participation because they voluntarily quit their most recent job or reduced their work effort below thirty (30) hours per week without good cause. True when /members/*/voluntarilyQuitOrReducedWorkEffort is true and /members/*/voluntaryQuitReason is set to Other (a reason was given but it does not fall within one of the enumerated 4.308.1 good cause categories) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308; 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Registered for work
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member registered for work at initial application and at every recertification by signing the application for assistance or recertification, either personally or through an authorized representative or another adult household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Provided employment status or availability information
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member provided the eligibility technician sufficient information regarding employment status or availability for work (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Accepted suitable employment offer
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member accepted any offer of suitable employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Reported to referred suitable employer
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member reported to an employer when referred by the local office and the potential employment was suitable employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Meets general work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member complies with the SNAP general work requirements by registering for work at application and recertification, providing sufficient information about employment status or availability for work, not committing an act of voluntary quit, accepting suitable employment, and reporting to a referred suitable employer when the potential employment is suitable (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work hours per week
Fact.Description: The average number of hours per week this member works (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for failure to cooperate with QA division
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for failure to cooperate with the state quality assurance division (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Physically or mentally unfit for employment for student eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether this member is physically or mentally unfit for employment for purposes of the SNAP student eligibility exemption. This student-specific flag is separate from the work-requirements unfitness determination so the two policy contexts can be captured independently (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Physically or mentally unfit for employment for work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this member is physically or mentally unfit for employment for purposes of SNAP work requirements. Examples include persons experiencing homelessness, persons recently released from an institution, persons with disabilities including self-declared temporary conditions preventing successful participation in work activities, persons receiving temporary or permanent disability benefits from government or private sources, persons participating in vocational rehabilitation, persons applying for or appealing SSI benefits, persons unable to maintain employment, and persons impacted by domestic violence (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Recently released from an institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member was recently released from an institution, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Has self-declared temporary condition preventing work activities
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a self-declared temporary condition that would prevent successful participation in work activities, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Receives temporary or permanent disability benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives temporary or permanent disability benefits issued by government or private sources, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is participating in vocational rehabilitation
Fact.Description: Whether this member is participating in vocational rehabilitation, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is applying for or appealing SSI benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member is applying for and/or appealing Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is unable to maintain employment
Fact.Description: Whether this member is unable to maintain employment, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is impacted by domestic violence
Fact.Description: Whether this member is impacted by domestic violence, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Enrolled in Employment and Training Program
Fact.Description: Whether this member is enrolled in the Employment and Training Program (Employment First/EF), a program operated by the Department of Human Services consisting of work, training, education, work experience, and/or job search activities designed to help clients obtain gainful employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: In on-the-job training
Fact.Description: Whether this member is receiving on-the-job training (OJT), training provided to an employee after he or she is hired, designed for individuals who do not have the necessary work experience required for the job (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is already participating in another household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is already receiving SNAP benefits as part of another SNAP household or in another state in the same calendar month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resident of a shelter for battered women and children
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of a public or private nonprofit residential facility that serves battered women and their children (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for participating in another household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified because they are already participating in another SNAP household in the same month. Residents of a shelter for battered women and children are exempt from this restriction (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for felony conviction non-compliance
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a person with a felony conviction who is not in compliance with the terms of their sentence and was convicted as an adult for conduct that occurred after February 7, 2014 for any of the following crimes: aggravated sexual abuse under Section 2241 of Title 18, United States Code; murder under Section 1111 of Title 18, United States Code; an offense under Chapter 110 of Title 18, United States Code; a federal or state offense involving sexual assault, as defined in Section 40002(a) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 13925(a)); or an offense under state law determined by the attorney general to be substantially similar to the foregoing (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for living in a boarding house or institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified because they are a resident of a commercial or noncommercial boarding house or an institution that has not been authorized by FNS to accept SNAP benefits, and they do not qualify for an exemption under Section 4.304.41 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for parole or probation violation
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified as a parole or probation violator. An impartial party designated by the agency must determine that the individual violated a condition of probation or parole imposed under federal or state law, and that federal, state, or local law enforcement authorities are actively seeking the individual to enforce those conditions. Active pursuit is established when a law enforcement agency informs the local office it intends to enforce an outstanding felony warrant or arrest the individual for a probation or parole violation within 20 days of submitting a request for information about the individual; presents a felony arrest warrant as provided in 4.304.4, B, 1; or states it intends to enforce an outstanding felony warrant or arrest the individual for a probation or parole violation within 30 days of the date of a request from a local office about a specific outstanding felony warrant or probation or parole violation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: ABAWD countable months limit
Fact.Description: The number of countable months an ABAWD may accrue within a thirty-six (36) month window before being disqualified (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Exceeded ABAWD countable months limit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ABAWD who has accrued at least the limit of countable months without meeting an exemption or ABAWD work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: E-EBT minimum payment
Fact.Description: The minimum Energy Electronic Benefit Transfer (E-EBT) fuel assistance payment that qualifies a SNAP household for the heating and cooling standard utility allowance (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Excess medical deduction
Fact.Description: A deduction from a household's total gross income applied when a person with a disability or a person aged sixty (60) and older has medical expenses over a specified monthly amount (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Substantial lottery or gambling winnings threshold
Fact.Description: A cash prize won in a single game, before taxes or other amounts are withheld, that is equal to or greater than this threshold counts as substantial lottery or gambling winnings. The threshold equals the resource limit for persons aged sixty (60) and older and persons with disabilities (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Largest lottery or gambling winnings this month
Fact.Description: The largest cash prize won by any household member in a single lottery or gambling game during the month, before taxes or other amounts are withheld (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Has substantial lottery or gambling winnings this month
Fact.Description: Whether the household's largest single-game lottery or gambling cash prize during the month equals or exceeds the substantial lottery or gambling winnings threshold. Such winnings from an individual will disqualify the entire SNAP household from eligibility in the month the winnings are received (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Had previous substantial lottery or gambling winnings
Fact.Description: Whether the SNAP household previously lost eligibility because a member received substantial lottery or gambling winnings. The next time such a household reapplies and is certified for SNAP after losing eligibility, the household must be considered under Standard Eligibility (SE) guidelines; after receiving SNAP as an SE household, the household will be re-evaluated for categorical eligibility at the next eligible certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Exempt income
Fact.Description: Income that is exempt from consideration when determining eligibility for SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Non-exempt earned income
Fact.Description: This member's earned income that is not exempt from consideration when determining eligibility for SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Unearned income
Fact.Description: This member's unearned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Currently equal to /members/*/sponsorIncome — the only unearned-income component modeled so far — so the value reflects the post-exemption sponsor income (deemed share or actual money paid, with the 4.000.1, E exemptions applied).

Fact.Name: Unearned income (including sponsor income)
Fact.Description: This member's unearned income for the indigent-non-citizen determination (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, E, 4). Mirrors /members/*/unearnedIncome but points at /members/*/deemedSponsorIncome — the raw per-non-citizen deemed share — instead of /members/*/sponsorIncome, so the indigence check uses sponsor income before the 4.000.1, E exemptions are applied and avoids cycling through /members/*/sponsorIncomeAndResourcesDoNotApply.

Fact.Name: Total self-employment income
Fact.Description: The household's total income received from self-operated businesses or enterprises in which the individual retains control over work or services offered and assumes the necessary business risks and expenses connected with the operation of the business (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Liquid resources
Fact.Description: Assets such as cash on hand or assets that can be easily converted to cash such as money in checking or savings accounts, saving certificates, or stocks and bonds (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Non-liquid resources
Fact.Description: The value of this member's non-liquid resources, such as personal effects, household goods, vehicles, buildings, land, and other real property (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resources
Fact.Description: This member's total countable resources, the sum of liquid resources, non-liquid resources, and any sponsor resources deemed to this member as a sponsored non-citizen (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Gross income
Fact.Description: The total of all non-exempt earned and unearned income added together before any deduction or disregard is considered (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Gross income (including sponsor income)
Fact.Description: This member's gross income with /members/*/unearnedIncomeWithSponsorIncome standing in for /members/*/unearnedIncome — i.e., using /members/*/deemedSponsorIncome (the raw per-non-citizen deemed share, NOT the post-exemption /members/*/sponsorIncome) as the sponsor-income contribution. Used to assess indigent non-citizen status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, E, 4) without cycling through /members/*/sponsorIncomeAndResourcesDoNotApply, since indigence itself feeds into that exemption umbrella.

Fact.Name: Net income test rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the net income test threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Net income threshold
Fact.Description: One hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, under which a household's income must fall after all allowable deductions are considered (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Net income
Fact.Description: The household's income after all allowable deductions are considered, used for the net income test (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Meets net income test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's net income falls at or below one hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Participates in Commodity Food Distribution Program
Fact.Description: Whether the household is on an Indian reservation and participating in the Commodity Food Distribution Program for the current period. Participation must be limited to either the Commodity Food Distribution Program or SNAP, not both (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4).

Fact.Name: Lives in application county or district
Fact.Description: Whether the household lives in the county or district in which they make application for the Program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Has nearby county/district filing arrangement
Fact.Description: Whether the local office has made arrangements to allow this household to file an application in a nearby specified county/district office (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Meets residency requirement
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the residency requirement: applicants shall live in the county or district in which they make application for the Program, unless the local office has made arrangements to allow particular households to file an application in a nearby specified county/district office (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Meets non-financial criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the set of rules other than those governing the household's gross and net income and resource standards (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is experiencing homelessness
Fact.Description: Whether this member lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence or whose primary residence is a supervised shelter designed for temporary accommodations; a halfway house or similar facility that provides temporary residence; a place not designed for or ordinarily used as regular sleeping accommodations for human beings; or a temporary accommodation in the residence of another individual for ninety (90) days or less (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is fleeing felon
Fact.Description: Whether this member is fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody for a crime, or an attempt to commit a crime, that would be classified as a felony under a state or federal law (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is migrant farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether this member travels away from home on a regular basis to follow the flow of seasonal agricultural work (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is striker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is involved in a strike or other concerted stoppage of work by employees, including a stoppage by reason of the expiration of a collective bargaining agreement and any concerted slowdown or other concerted interruption of operations by employees (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Was eligible for SNAP the day before the strike
Fact.Description: Whether the household containing this striking member was eligible for SNAP the day before the strike. A household containing a striker is only eligible for SNAP if the household was eligible the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of the strike (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Was exempt from work registration the day before the strike
Fact.Description: Whether this striking member was exempt from work registration the day before the strike, such as the caretaker of a child under six (6) years of age, other than persons exempt solely on the ground that they were employed. Households where the striking member was so exempt are not subject to the striker eligibility restriction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, A and D).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible striker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible striker. A household containing a striking member shall not be eligible for SNAP unless the household was eligible for the Program the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of the strike. Households where the striking member was exempt from work registration the day before the strike (other than persons exempt solely on the ground that they were employed) are not subject to these provisions (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Student enrollment status options
Fact.Description: Options describing a member's enrollment status in an institution of higher education — an institution that normally requires a high school diploma or equivalency certificate for a student to enroll, such as a college, university, or vocational or technical school: full time (a school schedule equivalent to a full-time curriculum as defined by the institution of higher education the person is attending), at least half time but less than full time, or less than half time / not enrolled (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Student enrollment status
Fact.Description: This member's enrollment status in an institution of higher education — an institution that normally requires a high school diploma or equivalency certificate for a student to enroll, such as a college, university, or vocational or technical school: full time (a school schedule equivalent to a full-time curriculum as defined by the institution of higher education the person is attending), at least half time but less than full time, or less than half time / not enrolled (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Enrolled in post high school education
Fact.Description: Whether this member is enrolled in a college, university, or post-high school level technical or vocational school (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is U.S. citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is considered a U.S. citizen for SNAP: a person born in the United States or in the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the Mariana Islands; a person who has become a citizen through the naturalization process; a person born outside the United States to at least one (1) U.S. citizen parent; or a child under eighteen (18) years of age adopted or born outside the U.S. with a parent who is a U.S. citizen, who has been admitted as a lawful permanent resident, and is in the legal and physical custody of a parent who is a U.S. citizen (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Is non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen — anyone who is not a U.S. citizen. Qualified non-citizens and certain groups of non-citizens who are not qualified are eligible for SNAP participation under certain conditions; some qualified non-citizens must also meet an additional condition to be eligible. Each category of qualified non-citizen stands alone for purposes of determining eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B).

Fact.Name: Is non-citizen national
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen national of the United States — an individual born in an outlying possession of the United States (either American Samoa or Swain's Island) on or after the date the U.S. acquired the possession, or a person whose parents are U.S. non-citizen nationals. Non-citizen nationals have eligibility for SNAP as U.S. citizens (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305)

Fact.Name: Is lawful permanent resident
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen legally admitted into the United States to reside on a permanent basis (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is parolee
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen granted parole into the United States, as described in 8 U.S.C. 1182(d)(5) and 8 C.F.R. 212.5 (2019). Parole does not constitute a formal admission to the United States and confers temporary status only, requiring parolees to leave when the conditions supporting their parole cease to exist (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is asylee
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen granted asylum, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is refugee
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen admitted as a refugee, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Has withholding of deportation or removal
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen granted withholding of deportation or removal, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is conditional entrant
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen admitted as a conditional entrant, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is Cuban or Haitian entrant
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a Cuban or Haitian entrant, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is battered immigrant
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a battered immigrant, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is victim of severe trafficking
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen victim of a severe form of trafficking, included as a qualified non-citizen for SNAP under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is Amerasian
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an Amerasian eligible for SNAP under 8 U.S.C. 1612, retroactive to August 22, 1996 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B).

Fact.Name: Is Iraqi or Afghan special immigrant
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an Iraqi or Afghan national granted special immigrant status under 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(27) for having worked on behalf of the U.S. Government in Iraq or Afghanistan. Under the Department of Defense Appropriations Act of 2010 (P.L. 111-118, Section 8120), Special Immigrant Visa holders are eligible for SNAP to the same extent and for the same period as refugees (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B).

Fact.Name: Is qualified non-citizen without additional condition
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a qualified non-citizen status that is eligible for SNAP participation indefinitely from the date the non-citizen obtains qualified non-citizen status or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status, without having to meet an additional condition: refugees admitted under 8 U.S.C. 1157, victims of trafficking under the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000, asylees granted asylum under Section 208 of the INA, non-citizens whose deportation or removal is being withheld under 8 U.S.C. 1224(H) or 8 U.S.C. 1231(B)(3), Cuban or Haitian entrants under 8 U.S.C. 1522(E), Amerasians under 8 U.S.C. 1612, and Iraqi or Afghan Special Immigrants under 8 U.S.C. 1101(A)(27) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 2, a).

Fact.Name: Is qualified non-citizen with additional condition
